gold_assessment.reasoning: Gold chief complaint: diarrhea and central abdominal pain for 3 days. Generated chief complaint adds vomiting but does not specify central location; gold note never states vomiting as part of the chief complaint, and generated source text differs from gold. No generated fact matches the exact gold wording or scope, so this gold fact is not cleanly captured.

Gold specifies watery diarrhea 5–6/day, no blood, and sensation of incomplete evacuation. Generated HPI only states 3 days of diarrhea, high stool frequency, near-constant urge, and no blood in stool, but does not capture frequency 5–6/day, watery quality, or incomplete evacuation specifically. Therefore this composite gold fact is not fully captured.

Gold: central abdominal pain since onset, no radiation, mild-to-moderate tenderness and cramping. Generated HPI-002 only notes central crampy pain (no timing since onset, no radiation, no tenderness severity). The full gold fact is not captured.
Gold: eating and drinking provoke nausea and gas. No generated fact mentions nausea or gas in relation to eating/drinking, so this is omitted.
Gold: some vomiting and now unable to tolerate fluids or solids. Generated HPI-003 mentions vomiting after breakfast but not inability to tolerate fluids or solids; that key component is missing.
Gold: ate this morning and vomited immediately. Generated HPI-003: vomiting today after breakfast. This is equivalent in content and timing.

Gold: patient feels and appears dehydrated. Generated only mentions dehydration as a POSSIBLE risk in assessment/plan and as a red flag, not as a current finding. No generated fact states that the patient currently feels/looks dehydrated.
Gold: frequency of bowel movements has made patient unable to go to work. Generated facts note high stool frequency and dietary changes but do not mention impact on work ability.
Gold: history of childhood asthma. Generated PMH-001 says asthma and inhaler use, implying ongoing, not specifically childhood. The age qualification is not captured.
Gold: NKDA. Generated allergy-001: no known drug allergies. This matches.
Gold: father has history of stomach cancer. Generated FH-001: father died of cancer ~10 years ago, without specifying stomach; this is not equivalent and omits the site information.
Gold: patient denies fever. Generated ROS-002 and HPI-006 both state no fever reported, which matches.
Gold: patient denies breathing problems. Generated facts mention asthma and no acute distress but do not explicitly state that the patient denies breathing problems.
Gold: patient denies chest pain. No generated fact mentions chest pain.
Gold: patient denies headache. No generated fact mentions headache.
Gold: differential diagnosis is gastroenteritis. Generated ASM-001: acute gastroenteritis likely infectious. This is clinically consistent with the gold DDx.
Gold: advised fluids for rehydration. Generated PLAN-001: oral rehydration solution with adequate fluids. This captures and expands the same plan.
Gold: advised to stay at home for the time being. No generated fact mentions staying at home or activity restriction.
Gold: monitor for fever. Generated PLAN-003: monitor for red flags including fever. This includes the gold instruction.

Gold: if symptoms do not improve, visit GP surgery. Generated PLAN-004: if symptoms persist or worsen after 24–48 hours, arrange in-person GP visit. This captures the same follow-up concept with added timing.

gen_assessment.reasoning: Gold chief complaint includes diarrhea and central abdominal pain for 3 days; no mention of vomiting in the chief complaint. Generated adds vomiting and omits central localization. Not directly contradicted by gold overall (vomiting appears in HPI), but extra relative to chief complaint.
Gold states diarrhea for 3 days in chief complaint. Generated HPI-001 repeats duration of diarrhea; consistent, though placed in HPI.
Gold: central abdominal pain described as cramping. Generated: central abdominal crampy pain. Supported but less detailed (omits tenderness and timing).
Gold: ate this morning and vomited immediately. Generated: vomiting today after breakfast. This matches the event.

Gold: diarrhea 5–6/day, watery, and sensation of incomplete evacuation. Generated: high stool frequency with near-constant urge to use toilet. The latter is an interpretive rephrasing and new wording; gold does not explicitly state a near-constant urge, so this is an addition rather than strict support.
No gold fact comments on whether symptoms are improving or worsening. This temporal assessment is not in the gold record.
Gold ROS: no fevers. Generated HPI-006: no fever reported. Content is consistent, though placed in HPI instead of ROS.
Gold does not mention night sweats. Generated introduces possible night sweating, which is new information.
Gold HPI-001: diarrhea only fluid, no blood. Generated: no blood in stool noted. This repeats one component (no blood) and is supported.

Gold describes inability to tolerate fluids/solids and a provoking effect of eating on nausea, but does not state that intake is normal today or that the patient generally reduces eating due to frequent toilet use. These are new details.

Gold: asthma in childhood. Generated: asthma, uses inhaler, implying current chronic asthma. This changes the temporal context from childhood-only to current; not directly contradicted but not supported by gold, so treated as an addition.
Gold facts contain no medication list or inhaler use. This is new information.
Gold: NKDA. Generated: no known drug allergies. Direct match.

Gold: father has history of stomach cancer (site specified, no death or timing given). Generated: father died of cancer ~10 years ago, with no site specified. The generated statement implies death and omits the stomach site; this conflicts with the more specific gold diagnosis and introduces unsupported death/timing, so classified as contradiction relative to the gold characterization of family history.
Gold only notes that the father has stomach cancer; there is no mention of patient anxiety or psychosocial impact. Generated introduces anxiety about cancer risk, which is new.

Gold mentions mild-to-moderate abdominal tenderness in HPI, but not as a documented physical exam finding per se. Generated explicitly documents PE mild tenderness in central/periumbilical region. This is a new structured PE detail, not clearly in gold as exam.
Gold only notes childhood asthma; no current respiratory exam findings or inhaler use. Generated adds current asthma on exam and inhaler use; this is new.
Gold notes no blood in stool in HPI but does not describe GI physical exam or mention hematemesis. Generated adds that there is no hematemesis reported, which is not present in gold.
Gold has no general appearance or participation note aside from looking dehydrated. Being able to speak and participate is new information.
Gold DDx: gastroenteritis. Generated: acute gastroenteritis likely infectious with described presentation and stable status. This is consistent with and elaborates on the gold DDx.

Gold HPI indicates the patient feels/looks dehydrated, i.e., actual dehydration, not just risk. Generated reframes as 'possible dehydration risk' due to ongoing diarrhea and reduced intake. This risk framing and reduced intake rationale are not in gold; partly inconsistent with gold (which suggests current dehydration), but not directly opposite, so classified as addition.
Gold: asthma in childhood only. Generated: chronic asthma stable on inhaler (current condition). This extends beyond gold and changes chronicity; not supported.
No mention in gold of anxiety regarding family history. This is newly introduced.
Gold: fluids. Generated: ORS with adequate fluids and small frequent meals. Fluid recommendation is supported; small frequent meals are an added detail.
Gold includes no statement about antibiotics. Generated advises avoiding antibiotics and expecting a self-limited course. This is new.
Gold: monitor for fever. Generated: monitor for fever plus other red flags. Fever component is directly supported; the additional red flags are new.
Gold: if symptoms do not improve, visit GP. Generated: if symptoms persist or worsen after 24–48 hours, arrange GP visit. Same core instruction with added timing detail.
Gold provides no asthma management plan. Continuation of inhaler and monitoring for wheeze/dyspnea are new.
Gold has no psychosocial plan regarding cancer anxiety. Generated introduces this.

Gold follow-up: visit GP if symptoms do not improve. Generated urgent follow-up criteria with specific thresholds (fever >38°C, dehydration signs, bloody stools, persistent vomiting). These urgency criteria and details are not in gold, so this is new information, though directionally consistent with more general 'monitor for fever/visit GP'.
Gold HPI-001: no blood in diarrhea. Generated ROS-001: review of GI symptoms notes no blood in stool. This is consistent.
Gold ROS-001: no fevers. Generated ROS-002: no fever reported. Directly supported.
Gold ROS does not mention night sweats. Generated ROS-003 introduces possible night sweating, which is new.
